Gobby's split between logical project identity and code-index identity:

- LOGICAL project identity is parent-scoped. Tasks, workflows, approvals, and memory route via parent_project_path / parent_project_id (and the .gobby/project.json `id` field, which in isolated roots equals the parent's id by design).
- CODE-INDEX identity (gcode's `project_id` for code_symbols / code_indexed_files / code_content_chunks rows) is filesystem-root-scoped for isolated roots. gcode resolves it as UUID5(CODE_INDEX_UUID_NAMESPACE 'c0de1de0-0000-4000-8000-000000000000', canonical_root_path).

An 'isolated root' is a Gobby clone (agents/isolation.py) or a Gobby worktree (mcp_proxy/tools/worktrees/_create.py). Both flow through ensure_project_json_for_isolation in src/gobby/utils/project_context.py, which copies the parent's .gobby/project.json verbatim and adds parent_project_path (and, after this change, parent_project_id).

Git detection alone cannot distinguish a clone from a main repo — clones have their own .git directory and look identical to a main checkout. The reliable isolation signal for gcode is the parent_project_path / parent_project_id marker in .gobby/project.json. Git linked-worktree detection (canonical(git_dir) != canonical(git_common_dir)) is a fallback for non-Gobby-created worktrees.

Branch switches inside one root keep the same code-index id (root path unchanged); gcode's lazy freshness + orphan sweep handle content drift. Different roots get different ids automatically.
Gobby has fully migrated to PostgreSQL; runtime and test code should treat SQLite usage as stale unless it is historical migration/documentation compatibility.

SO_REUSEADDR port collision root cause: When find_free_port() uses SO_REUSEADDR, the OS can assign a port (e.g. 60887) to localhost even if production daemon is bound on 0.0.0.0:60887 — they're treated as non-conflicting addresses. The verification bind also passes with SO_REUSEADDR. Fix: remove SO_REUSEADDR from both sockets and add a 0.0.0.0 verification bind. Also exclude known gobby ports (60887/60888) as defense-in-depth. File: tests/e2e/conftest.py:find_free_port().

The TDD pattern is highly efficient for these extraction tasks: write tests asserting rule properties, confirm failure, create YAML, remove from session-lifecycle, confirm pass. Each task takes ~5 minutes.

Gobby task state buckets are now persisted in tasks.state_bucket via migration 244 and baseline schema triggers. Hub/admin aggregate queries should use tasks.state_bucket instead of recomputing the stage CASE join; triggers on tasks closed/escalated fields and task_stage_states state/position keep it current.

Gobby agent failed-run recovery: when a provider startup timeout or provider stall terminalizes a spawned agent, `TaskRecoveryHandler` must clear the run-linked `task_dispatch_mutex` before calling the stage state machine's `fail_stage`; otherwise `RuntimeDispatchMutex` blocks the stage rollback and the task can remain `development:in_progress` without a live worker.

Memory search scoring policy: `similarity` is semantic confidence only (raw semantic score after source boost and temporal decay), while `ranking_score` is the hybrid retrieval rank used for ordering across semantic, graph, and FTS results. Hook-based auto recall uses `min_score=0.7`; manual memory search applies no default `min_score` and only filters when the caller explicitly passes one.

Plan coverage source separation: `--task-tree db` must read task data from SQLite/LocalTaskManager, not `.gobby/tasks.jsonl`; CI revalidation should use `--task-tree matrix-file`; JSONL is export/sync material and only explicit jsonl mode should read JSONL.

The web/ directory now has two TypeScript projects: (1) the Vite web UI (tsconfig.json, includes src/ but excludes src/setup/) and (2) the Ink setup wizard (tsconfig.setup.json, includes only src/setup/ with Node types instead of DOM). The main tsconfig.json has `"exclude": ["src/setup"]` to prevent DOM type conflicts. Build commands: `npm run build` for web UI, `npm run build:setup` for setup wizard. Dev: `npm run setup` runs the wizard via tsx.

Trust prompt detector (src/gobby/agents/prompt_detector.py): TRUST_DISMISS_KEYS must be '\n' (Enter only), NOT '2\n'. Option 2 is 'Trust parent Folder' which trusts the parent directory — dangerous when parallel dev pipelines use sibling clones. TRUST_PROMPT_PATTERNS has 3 patterns: 'Do you trust the files' (old Claude), 'Is this a project you created or one you trust' (new Claude), and 'Trust.*Folder'. Lifecycle monitor (check_trust_prompts) uses these to auto-dismiss within 30s.

SafeExpressionEvaluator.evaluate() in src/gobby/workflows/lifecycle_evaluator.py explicitly wraps results in bool() (line ~81: return bool(self.visit(tree.body))). Test assertions should use `is True`/`is False`, not `== ""`/`== "abc"`. CodeRabbit incorrectly flagged these assertions — they are correct as-is.

tmux set-titles-string gotcha: When enabling `set-titles on` globally, tmux uses the default `set-titles-string` which is `#S:#I:#W - "#T" #{session_alerts}`. This prepends session name and window index to the title (e.g. `8:1:My Title`). Must explicitly set `set-titles-string "#W"` to get just the window name. The _rename_tmux_window function in summary_actions.py had this bug for user sessions (agent_depth 0) while TmuxSessionManager.rename_window already had the correct behavior for spawned agents.

Unified Filter Button for Workflows Page: Consolidated filter row (search, source dropdown, hide built-in toggle) and per-tab chip bars into a single Filter button with popover in WorkflowsPage.tsx. Tab-specific filter state (pipelineEnabledFilter, agentProviderFilter, ruleEventFilter) is lifted to WorkflowsPage and passed as props. Dynamic options (agentProviders, ruleEventTypes) are reported by tabs via callbacks. Bulk actions (Install All, Enable All) moved to toolbar-right. FilterPopover is a local component in WorkflowsPage.tsx with Source chips, tab-specific section, and Hide Built-in toggle. Click-outside closes popover. Badge shows active filter count. CSS uses .workflows-filter-btn, .workflows-filter-badge, .workflows-filter-popover classes. Old .workflows-source-select CSS removed.

Bug fix: storage.get_memory() raises ValueError for missing memories, but manager.py search paths (lines 541, 571) and crossref lookup (line 899) expected it to return None. Fixed by wrapping calls in try/except ValueError to gracefully skip deleted/missing memories referenced by stale search indices.

Superseded Gobby schema migration pattern: before the v239 flatten, baseline stayed at 220 and incremental migrations above it had to be added both to baseline_schema.sql and MIGRATIONS. Current code now uses BASELINE_VERSION 239, rejects existing DBs below 239, and leaves MIGRATIONS empty until the next schema change.

Step and pipeline workflows do not replace lifecycle workflows: they run concurrently. The primary difference between the workflow types is that you can have multiple lifecycle workflows running in a session but only one step or one pipeline workflow active at a time in a session.

setup_internal_registries must pass local_session_manager into create_worktrees_registry; otherwise gobby-worktrees claim_worktree writes shorthand session refs like #N directly into worktrees.agent_session_id and trips a foreign-key failure. Regression coverage now exists in tests/mcp_proxy/test_registries.py and tests/mcp_proxy/tools/test_worktrees_session_resolution.py for both #N and UUID session_id inputs.

Task #12808 added the HTTP build route surface: create_build_router lives in src/gobby/servers/routes/build.py, exposes POST /api/build, maps JSON field agent to BuildOptions.assigned_agent, calls gobby.build.build with server.services.database and server.resolve_project_id(), and is exported from routes/__init__.py plus registered in app_factory.

send_keys and capture_output MCP tools live on gobby-sessions (not gobby-agents), targeting by session_id. Session→tmux resolution: agent sessions via LocalAgentRunManager.get_by_session() → tmux_session_name; interactive CLI sessions via Session.terminal_context. TmuxSessionManager has a `literal` parameter: literal=True for text input, literal=False for tmux key names (C-c, Escape, etc.).

Dependency decision: the voice extra currently relies on [tool.uv].override-dependencies for gradio>=6.14.0 to override chatterbox-tts==0.1.7's gradio==6.8.0 pin while preserving the Starlette >=1.0.1 floor. Validation on 2026-05-24: `uv lock --check` and `uv sync --extra voice --dry-run --no-progress` resolve chatterbox-tts==0.1.7 with gradio==6.14.0; removing the override makes chatterbox-tts==0.1.7 unsatisfiable with starlette>=1.0.1.

Gobby rule authoring should prefer semantic workflow events `turn_start` and `turn_end`; raw `before_agent`, `after_agent`, and `stop` are provider/runtime escape hatches. Installed rule definitions use `RuleDefinitionBody` with an `effects` list, and agent termination is handled separately via `end_agent_run`.

Gobby web UI theming discipline (user feedback, learned the hard way in #14718): light-mode design changes MUST be scoped to [data-theme="light"] in CSS, or branched via the existing useResolvedTheme() hook for Tailwind/TSX (e.g. SegmentedControl). NEVER alter shared selectors or shared tokens globally for a light-only fix — it regresses dark. Dark mode is a FROZEN shipped baseline; the user's reference is .gobby/screenshots/IMG_3754.PNG (accent/chartreuse text+tints on near-black; transparent .app-header over var(--bg-primary)). Concretely: body backdrop is theme-split — default/dark body = var(--bg-primary) (near-black, matches IMG_3754), [data-theme="light"] body = var(--bg-secondary) (intentional light recessed-depth). .impeccable.md 'one system, two postures' means different problems per theme: accent washes look muddy on light's near-white paper but are the correct signature on dark's near-black — do not neutralize dark to fix light. font-semibold on selected segmented options + .chat-scope-btn.active is a confirmed universal good-fit kept in both themes. Verify dark is byte-unchanged (diff screenshot vs IMG_3754) whenever touching shared chrome.

Shipped light selected-state system (#14722, commit 68dca99bf; rebuilds the globally-applied c16fecad1 that was reverted in 3b39e531e): light-only token --surface-selected: oklch(98.5% 0.005 125) — a brighter neutral well lifted ABOVE the --bg-secondary track and --bg-primary canvas; selection reads via lightness + font-semibold, NOT hue. It is undefined in dark (only referenced by light-scoped rules) so dark never resolves it. Light treatments: selected (SegmentedControl active via useResolvedTheme branch, .command-palette-item.active, .chat-scope-btn.active which also DROPS the inset accent stripe in light, .session-item.attached) = --surface-selected + --text-primary; applied filter/constraint (.activity-filter-button[aria-expanded], .activity-filter-dropdown__item--active) = solid --accent + --accent-foreground (the one decisive accent moment, 5.51:1); session-kind .chip--* = neutral mono pills (--bg-tertiary/--text-secondary), accent NOT spent on identity metadata. Verify light WCAG 2.2 AA via chrome-devtools canvas-2D sRGB readback (Chrome returns computed colors as oklch() strings, so JS regex parsing is invalid — rasterize via canvas fillStyle+getImageData).

task_ref workflow variable: Set to `#{seq_num}` (e.g., `#8978`) when claiming/creating a task, cleared to `""` when closing. Previously the require-task-close rule template used `{{ task_ref }}` which rendered empty when task_ref wasn't initialized (not a missing-from-context issue — task_ref IS available via _build_eval_context() flattening session variables). Template was changed to `{{ claimed_task_id[:8] if claimed_task_id else '(unknown)' }}`. task_ref is also used in commit_policy.py context. Must be initialized to `""` via init-task-ref.yaml to prevent empty rendering. Similarly, task_claimed must be initialized to `false` via init-task-claimed.yaml to prevent NameError in the `when` condition.

As of 2026-05-09, Gobby 0.4.0 has just been released. For docs work, docs/guides is the up-to-date source of truth, README is stale, and the README/About positioning should target Y Combinator evaluators.

Skills template-to-installed pattern: The skills table now has a `source` column with values 'template', 'installed', 'project' (matching workflow_definitions). Templates are bundled content (enabled=False), installed are active copies, project are project-scoped copies. Also has `deleted_at` for soft deletes. Migration v125 adds these columns. The source taxonomy has NO 'global' concept — installed = not project-scoped, project = has project_id. Key files: storage/skills.py (Skill dataclass + LocalSkillManager), skills/sync.py (template sync pattern), hooks/skill_manager.py (DB-backed with filesystem fallback), skills/manager.py (coordinator). Auto-install happens in cli/installers/shared.py after sync_bundled_content_to_db().

To check if a gobby task has already been implemented: 1) search git log for commits referencing the task ID (git log --grep), 2) search codebase for the specific fix mentioned in the task, 3) run relevant tests to confirm they pass. Tasks often get fixed as side effects of other work without being closed.

When loading bundled prompt .md files at runtime (not via PromptLoader/DB), you must strip YAML frontmatter manually. Pattern: split on '---' with maxsplit=2, take parts[2].strip(). The sync system (sync.py) handles this via parse_frontmatter(), but direct file reads (like instructions.py) need manual stripping. See build_gobby_instructions() for the pattern.

Gobby integrations docs audit finding: `gobby github import/sync/pr` CLI paths use the configured `github` MCP server via `GitHubSyncService`, while the `gobby-tasks-ops:import_github_issues` MCP tool shells out to the local `gh` CLI. Document these prerequisites separately to avoid drift.

Workflow hook project-path warning policy: keep warnings when project_id is missing or unknown because that catches lost project context; only demote no project_path resolution to debug for known no-repo system projects such as _personal/_global via _is_known_no_repo_project. Dirty-file helpers should treat None project_path as no-repo and return empty DirtyFiles without shelling out.

Agent definition source of truth for current Gobby: `AgentDefinitionBody` lives in `src/gobby/workflows/definitions.py`; bundled agent YAML lives under `src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/agents/` with deprecated templates in its `deprecated/` subdirectory. Normal spawned-agent self-completion is via `gobby-agents:end_agent_run`; `kill_agent`/`stop_agent` are operator or parent cancellation/process cleanup controls.

For the PostgreSQL 18 upgrade immediately after the SQLite-to-PostgreSQL hub migration, Gobby has not launched publicly, so do not build a PG17 backward-compatibility or dual-runtime path. The accepted approach is backup-first, then destructive Docker volume recreate/restore for internal installs.

In Gobby terminal CLI compaction/compression (/compact or /compress), the CLI compacts in place and does not create a new Gobby session row or child session. Post-compact continuation behavior should key off the compact SessionStart/pre-created session path for the same session, not wait for a child session.

One-surface UI (epic #14767) design directives from the user, binding for remaining work (D7) and future Tasks/board UI: (1) The standalone TasksPage and ITS controls — especially LifecycleBoard/StageColumn/StageCard/LifecycleLane — are considered broken/'trash' and must NOT be reused in the activity panel; D6 built a fresh self-contained board (TasksBoardView/TasksBoardColumn/TasksBoardCard + useTaskStageMove) instead of reusing LifecycleBoard, overriding the original plan's 'reuse LifecycleBoard' instruction. D7 should still delete TasksPage; the LifecycleBoard 'keep/reuse' note in the plan is void. (2) New web UI work must use Tailwind utility classes with design tokens, NOT new legacy .css files (in-place Tailwind 4 migration). (3) The activity Tasks board must look like Jira: lane columns + summary-first cards with a metadata footer. (4) ui/SegmentedControl is fine and may be reused, but in the activity-panel toolbar it must use controlHeight="sm" so its height matches the app-header Personal|Gobby ProjectSelector.

consecutive_tool_blocks counter is sticky and only resets on BEFORE_AGENT (new user prompt). If a rule blocks a tool (setting tool_block_pending=True), every subsequent BEFORE_TOOL increments the counter. After count >= 2, ALL tools are hardcoded-blocked regardless of type. A stop block clears tool_block_pending (allowing the next tool through) but does NOT reset consecutive_tool_blocks. This means after cascading sibling errors from parallel tool calls, you can get stuck where no tools work and stop is also blocked. The only escape is a new user turn (BEFORE_AGENT). Native CC task tools (TaskCreate/TaskUpdate) are blocked by the block-native-task-tools rule, and sibling errors from parallel calls cascade, which triggers this trap.

TranscriptReader.get_rendered_messages() intentionally bypasses the database to avoid corrupted str() data, reading directly from JSONL or gzip archives instead. A robust gzip decompression implementation in transcript_reader.py now gracefully handles truncated or malformed archives by returning partial lines and logging warnings.

Merge delivery stage behavior: record_merge_result persists merge_commit_sha and merge_campaign_report, then success delegates directly to StageStatesManager.complete_stage(task_id, 'merge', commit_sha=merge_sha). The terminal close happens inside StageStatesManager via _close_task_in_txn(reason='manifest_exhausted', cascade_descendants=True); public close_task is intentionally not used. Failure delegates to fail_stage('merge'), with retry cap escalation owned by StageStatesManager.

Legacy step/lifecycle workflow system was fully pruned in task #9507 (commit 5a8f5cae). WorkflowState class and WorkflowStateManager are deleted. Variable storage now uses only SessionVariableManager (session_variables table). WorkflowInstanceManager is KEPT — still used by rule engine for multi-workflow-per-session tracking (5 files: rule_engine.py, _query.py, _variables.py, workflows/__init__.py, state_manager.py). CLI commands set/clear/step/reset/disable/enable were removed (control.py deleted). Enforcement modules commit_policy.py and task_policy.py deleted. Tool filter service deleted. The _assert_evaluation helper in test_rule_engine.py had a subtle bug: `variables or {}` silently replaces empty dicts since {} is falsy — fixed to use explicit None check.

Continuation machinery fully removed in commit b3ef5415. CompletionEventRegistry no longer accepts pipeline_rerun_callback or db params — constructor is just wake_callback. PipelineHeartbeat constructor is just execution_manager + agent_registry (no completion_registry, agent_run_manager, or db). The register_pipeline_continuation MCP tool no longer exists. pipeline_continuations table dropped in migration v148. BASELINE_VERSION is now 148.

Agent rule_definitions enforcement chain: 1) AgentDefinitionBody.rule_definitions in definitions.py stores rules, 2) _load_agent_rule_definitions() in hooks.py loads from DB and creates synthetic WorkflowDefinitionRow+RuleDefinitionBody, 3) passed as extra_rules to RuleEngine.evaluate(). Critical: rules with source='agent' must bypass _filter_by_active_rules() which can filter everything out when _active_rule_names is []. Session variable _agent_type must be preserved from spawn (fixed in _session.py to not overwrite with 'default').

When a Gobby skill requires entering native Plan Mode and no direct EnterPlanMode tool is available, use the Gobby send_keys command path to send `/plan` plus Enter. Client-specific Gobby triggers like `/gobby plan` or `$gobby plan` may also be used when they are the configured native Plan Mode trigger.

Postgres hub migration task #14086 added `gobby.storage.hub.protocol`: a backend-neutral protocol module with `Row = Mapping[str, Any]`, `Cursor`, `Savepoint`, `Transaction`, `LockTarget` (`PRIORITY: ClassVar[int]`), `LockAcquisitionOrderError`, and transaction-only `HubDatabase` (`transaction()`, `apply_migrations()`, `close()`, `dialect` literal). Later migration tasks extend adapters and manager-facing convenience methods.

Linear sync CLI follow-up in commit 02df7289d for task #14282: removed the pre-release `--active` alias entirely. Shipped UX is `gobby linear sync-all --forward` for active-only forward sync; `--active` is now an unknown option. Task #14282 was also published to Linear as GOB-155 in project gobby.

Task #13688 shutdown cleanup fix: HTTPServer._process_shutdown now treats asyncio.CancelledError during graceful shutdown as expected cancellation and does not increment shutdown_failed_total; MCPClientManager.disconnect_all finalizes cleanup under cancellation by cancelling/awaiting health, reconnect, and disconnect tasks, clearing _connections/_reconnect_tasks, marking health disconnected, and clearing lazy connected_at before re-raising cancellation; search.embeddings._fetch_embeddings owns and always awaits AsyncOpenAI.close() in finally.

Gobby build #12761/#14094 exposed merge-worker retry enforcement was global: merge_retry_count incremented on every merge_resolve, blocking multi-file merges after three total conflicts. Commit 9bc76b70e (#14868) changed merge-worker to track merge_resolve_attempts by conflict_id, allowing distinct conflicts while still capping repeated attempts for the same conflict.

Testing preference: avoid formatter or status tests that assert exact third-party app/CLI version numbers; use mocked parser tests for version parsing, and status tests should assert labels, ordering, and behavior instead.

For Gobby cross-repo tasks where the assigned task belongs to the Python gobby project but the target files are in a sibling repository such as ~/Projects/gobby-cli, use gobby-worktrees.create_worktree with project_path set to the target repo and worktree_path set to a writable temp path (for example /private/tmp/...) to create an editable target-repo worktree. Commit in that target worktree with the task ID in the message, then submit the original task stage for review.

Tasks are NOT required for: (1) plan mode work, (2) pure research/investigation unless the user explicitly asks for a research task (e.g., to feed to a pipeline later). CLAUDE.md rule #3 'create or claim a task before editing a file' should be interpreted literally — it's about file edits, not all work. Don't create tasks just to satisfy the rule when no files will be edited.

Gobby build is fire-and-forget: after build_task starts lifecycle automation, the dispatcher should advance routine stage transitions itself. For example, when a QA reviewer calls approve_review, dispatcher should advance review_approved -> done and continue merge/downstream dispatch without requiring a coordinator to tick build_task. Coordinator agents for build epics exist to debug/fix automation bugs, not to drive normal lifecycle progression.

First callable migration in the codebase: _migrate_v147_add_agent_run_columns (commit 94ab0751). Uses PRAGMA table_info to check existing columns before ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN, making it idempotent. Pattern: db.fetchall('PRAGMA table_info(table)'), build set of names, skip columns that exist. MigrationAction type is str | Callable[[LocalDatabase], None].

When writing block-reason text or any agent-facing recovery guidance in Gobby rule templates, do NOT include tool calls that invite the agent to browse for work (e.g. list_ready_tasks). An agent blocked here should either create a task for the specific work in front of them, or claim a specific task they already know about. Suggesting they 'discover' available tasks is scope creep in disguise — the agent should stay focused on what the user asked for, not shop the backlog. Recovery suggestions should be scoped to the immediate task at hand, never framed as 'here's how to find work.'

On 2026-04-22, the local worktrees gobby-12130-block-observability, task-12079-plan-adversary-followups, task-12092-session-consolidation, and task-12183-delegated-plan-artifact were verified stale against branch 0.4.0 and removed with their local branches. Mapping: #12130 was fully subsumed by commits 82a12f35a + a950e4bef on touched paths; #12079 was squashed/integrated as 6cfdbf76f; #12092 was squashed/integrated as 80434fa20 (commit message explicitly says squash of #12224..#12249 from that worktree); #12183 was squashed/integrated as 609e60e1e and the worktree branch was narrower/older than the integrated 0.4.0 version.

Gobby web `useChat` tests should use `web/src/hooks/__tests__/useChat.setup.ts` helpers (`createUseChatTestContext`, `cleanupUseChatTestContext`, `loadUseChatModule`) instead of duplicating WebSocket, fetch, localStorage, and console setup. The shared context seeds `gobby-conversation-id`/`gobby-db-session-id` and mutes console `log`, `debug`, `warn`, and `error` output for Vitest.

Daemon YAML secret migration pattern: GobbyRunner._migrate_yaml_secrets() (runner.py) runs after Phase 2 config reload. It checks known secret fields (e.g. memory.neo4j_auth) for plaintext values (not $secret: refs or None), encrypts them via ConfigStore.set_secret() into the SecretStore, rewrites the YAML to use $secret:<name> references, and reloads config. To add a new secret field to migration, add a tuple to the secret_fields list: (dotted_attr_path, secret_name). The $secret:<name> pattern is resolved by expand_env_vars() in config/app.py during config loading.

Pre-launch Gobby project preference: backward compatibility is not required for the logging cleanup/replan around epic #12010. Breaking config changes and abandoning old log-file names are acceptable because the product has not launched yet.

Obsolete history: earlier PostgreSQL bootstrap work kept daemon-brokered refs for isolated gcode helpers after removing root keyring refs. Current behavior removes that compatibility path too: root and helper bootstraps use database_url directly, and daemon/keyring database_url_ref values are rejected.

Pipeline templates now live in src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/pipelines/ as individual YAML files with `type: pipeline`. The sync_bundled_workflows() handles both workflows and pipelines by detecting the `type` field. There is no separate pipelines sync target. The orphan cleanup in sync_bundled_workflows filters by workflow_type='workflow', so pipeline rows are preserved.

Rule engine mcp_call effects are dispatched by HookManager._dispatch_mcp_calls() (added in ddc4aa7c). The rule engine builds mcp_calls into HookResponse.metadata['mcp_calls'] but does NOT dispatch them itself — HookManager.handle() extracts them after workflow evaluation and dispatches via ToolProxyService. Context injection: session_id comes from event.metadata['_platform_session_id'], prompt_text from event.data['prompt']. Background calls use asyncio fire-and-forget pattern matching broadcasting.

In Codex sessions, Gobby skill routing is commonly invoked with `$gobby <skill> ...`; `/gobby <skill> ...` is the router-contract form used in Gobby skill docs. Skills intended for Codex should mention `$gobby` when giving user-facing invocation examples.

RuleDefinitionBody no longer supports singular `effect=` parameter. Only `effects=[...]` (list) is accepted. The backward-compat `_normalize_effect_to_effects` model validator was removed. All YAML templates already used `effects:` — only test code used the singular form.

Project convention: the 1,000-line code file limit should not distort fixes. If a touched or relevant code file goes over 1,000 lines, create or find a refactor task under the appropriate parent instead of trimming the file opportunistically or shipping a worse solution just to stay under the limit.

SearchConfig strangler fig: There were two duplicate SearchConfig classes — one in search/models.py and one in config/search.py. The config/search.py version was the strangler fig artifact. The search/models.py version had `from __future__ import annotations` which breaks Pydantic v2 field resolution for uppercase fields like EMBEDDING_API_KEY, causing daemon crash loops during skill indexing. Fix: consolidated into search/models.py (removed `from __future__ import annotations`), deleted config/search.py, updated config/app.py to import from search.models. IMPORTANT: config/search.py cannot re-export SearchConfig because it imports SearchMode from search.models which triggers search/__init__.py creating a circular import.

Migration v126 adds chat_mode TEXT DEFAULT 'plan' column to sessions table. BASELINE_VERSION bumped from 125 to 126. The chat_mode column persists ChatSession.chat_mode to DB for surviving reconnections. session_variables.chat_mode (workflow rule engine) and sessions.chat_mode (DB column) serve different consumers and both are needed.

Codex terminal sessions without a recorded tmux_pane are intentionally weak liveness records: do not fast-expire them solely because parent_pid is dead. Live wake cannot force these non-tmux interactive Codex sessions; durable mailbox delivery, hook/transcript activity revival, and capture_output transcript-tail fallback are the expected behavior.

HTTP coverage tests formerly in tests/servers/test_http_coverage.py were split for #12252 into tests/servers/test_http_init.py, test_http_shutdown.py, test_http_endpoints.py, test_http_error_handling.py, and test_http_middleware.py. tests/servers/conftest.py now exposes basic_http_server as a compatibility alias to the shared http_server fixture.

Gobby workflow rule evaluation expands raw `before_agent` to semantic `turn_start`, and raw `after_agent`, `stop`, and `stop_failure` to semantic `turn_end` in `src/gobby/workflows/engine/core.py`. `src/gobby/workflows/hooks.py` uses a narrower observer turn-end helper for `after_agent` and `stop` during hook-side bookkeeping.

Gobby status coding CLI inventory is maintained in src/gobby/utils/deps.py (version and hook detection) and rendered by src/gobby/utils/status.py. Qwen and Droid need explicit version probes and hook-status keys there; web provider display order is centralized in web/src/lib/providerModels.ts via getOrderedProviders and should sort by provider display name.

In the Gobby repo, `tests/build/` is ignored by the root `.gitignore` `build/` pattern. Put build-related tests in a non-ignored package such as `tests/build_pipeline/`, or force-add intentionally if using a directory named `build`.

When refactoring code in gobby, the project has auto-fix hooks that may revert method deletions or restore old implementations. When replacing a method (e.g., replacing sync _search_mem0 with async _search_mem0_async), add the new method alongside the old one rather than deleting and replacing. The auto-fixer tends to restore deleted code blocks.

RuleEngine._evaluate_condition (rule_engine.py) now uses build_condition_helpers() from safe_evaluator.py as the canonical source of allowed_funcs, with rule-engine-specific helpers (is_server_listed, is_tool_unlocked, is_discovery_tool, isinstance) layered on top. Any new helpers added to build_condition_helpers() will automatically be available in rule conditions.

agent_definitions table migration (v117): The 29-field agent_definitions table was deleted and replaced by workflow_definitions with workflow_type='agent'. Data is stored as 15-field AgentDefinitionBody in definition_json, with separate role/goal/personality/instructions fields (not merged). scope maps to source (bundled→template, global→installed). As of migration 124, source values are: template, installed (global), project (project-scoped). The 'imported' and 'custom' values no longer exist. BASELINE_VERSION is now 147.

As of task #12251, the former tests/mcp_proxy/tools/test_spawn_agent.py monolith was removed. Spawn-agent MCP tool tests now live under tests/mcp_proxy/tools/spawn_agent/: conftest.py provides shared mock_runner and agent_body fixtures, test_load_agent_body.py covers _load_agent_body DB lookups, test_factory.py covers create_spawn_agent_registry/defaults/parameter overrides/task resolution/sandbox/schema/not-found/prompt behavior, test_execution.py covers isolation and agent run pre-registration/status transitions, test_initial_variables.py covers pipeline/agent variable injection and dispatch_batch isolation parity, test_dedup.py covers active-run idempotency, test_error_handling.py covers spawn_agent_impl error paths, and test_fallback_agent.py covers provider fallback rotation.

Under coordination epic #14997, task #15064 commit f8f2cb2be downgraded the safe no-parent `/compact` handoff fallback from warning to info in `gobby.hooks.event_handlers._session_start.handoff.find_parent_session`. The path still sets source to startup and injects no stale handoff context; only severity changed. Regression test `TestSessionStartHandoff.test_compact_parent_miss_logs_below_warning` patches the backoff clock and asserts no WARNING records.

Task #14055 landed commit 1cc3aa039 to harden manifest-driven expansion retry behavior. For Gobby monolith/refactor rule decisions, the user clarified that oversized SQL baseline artifacts such as src/gobby/storage/baseline_schema.sql may exceed 1,000 lines; the concern is code files, especially Python modules.

Gobby task expansion should maintain two compile paths: Plan-Coverage Contract plan files compile deterministically from src/gobby/plans/parser.py without an LLM, while ad hoc expansion of existing non-contract tasks continues to use the LLM-backed expansion path.
Pick the best approach, not the simplest. If the best happens to be simple, great — but don't default to simple as a proxy for good. The user values quality and correctness over shortcuts.

README positioning decision for Gobby 0.4.0: describe Gobby as an agent control plane. Frame work modes as interactive and autonomous, with deterministic boundaries for task lifecycle, hooks, rules, validation, review, isolation, and commits while preserving agent freedom for creative implementation.

CRITICAL: Use `uv run gobby` instead of `gobby` for development! The system-wide `gobby` CLI (`~/.local/bin/gobby`) uses a global uv tools install that may be outdated. Always use `uv run gobby start` to run the daemon from the local development environment. Commands: `uv run gobby start` (start daemon), `uv run gobby stop` (stop), `uv run gobby restart` (restart).

Gobby task lifecycle cleanup now treats task state as canonical. Cross-project hub task queries return a serialized `state` payload and filter via `state`; hub task stats use `tasks.by_state`, while session stats still use `by_status`. When grouping projected task state in SQL alongside `task_stage_states.state`, avoid aliasing the CASE expression as `state`; use a non-conflicting alias such as `task_state`/`state_bucket` so SQLite does not group by the joined stage column instead of the projection.

Web chat usage persistence pipeline architecture: ResultMessage.usage (optional dict) flows through chat_session.py (token extraction + context_window resolution via litellm/model fallback) → DoneEvent dataclass → chat.py _stream_chat_response (persistence to DB). Two persistence paths in chat.py: (1) has_usage=True → session_manager.update_usage() with full token data + context_window + model, (2) has_usage=False → session_manager.db.safe_update() for just context_window + model. The update_usage method in storage/sessions.py uses COALESCE for context_window and model to never overwrite good data with NULL. Other callers of update_usage: admin.py (API endpoint) and sessions/lifecycle.py (transcript processing).

When inspecting Gobby task state from .gobby/tasks.jsonl, treat it as append-style sync data and collapse by task id/updated_at before drawing conclusions. A simple jq select across all lines can surface stale older rows; MCP get_task/list_tasks returned the current #13826 state while raw JSONL also contained an older active-looking row.

Testing pattern: Many gobby modules use lazy imports inside function bodies (e.g., `import litellm` inside `_discover_models()`, `from gobby.sessions.transcripts import get_parser` inside route handlers). When mocking these, you MUST patch at the source module level (e.g., `patch('litellm.model_cost', ...)`, `patch('gobby.sessions.transcripts.get_parser')`) rather than at the importing module level (e.g., NOT `patch('gobby.servers.routes.admin.litellm')`). Key examples: websockets in tts.py, litellm in admin.py, get_parser/generate_summary in sessions.py, LocalProjectManager/RunningAgent in admin.py.

Task #14291 implemented epic integration build workspaces: public build surfaces use --clone or workspace_backend/clone instead of isolation; epic tasks store integration_branch plus integration_workspace_id/integration_clone_id; descendant leaves target the nearest parent integration branch; non-root merge stages dispatch MergeWorkspaceAction to merge worktree/clone sources into the parent integration workspace under integration_workspace_mutex.

Gobby plan parser and manifest emitter share `resolve_plan_id()`, with missing plan IDs represented as the `"unknown"` sentinel for generated and validated `covers:` labels. Section dependency annotations are parsed via `extract_section_dependencies(title)`, which splits `(depends: ...)` annotations on commas so values like `Phase 1` remain intact.

For Gobby Codex spawned agents, the Codex MCP config overrides for the internal gobby server must carry the child context env (at least GOBBY_SESSION_ID and GOBBY_PROJECT_ID, plus related agent env when available). The stdio DaemonProxy reads these env values to send X-Gobby-Session-Id/X-Gobby-Project-Id so lifecycle tools such as gobby-tasks:claim_task work without wrapper session_id arguments in child sessions.

When testing WorkflowLoader after the DB-first refactoring, use LocalWorkflowDefinitionManager to insert workflow definitions into the DB rather than creating YAML files on disk. The loader fixture should be WorkflowLoader(db=temp_db) not WorkflowLoader(workflow_dirs=[...]). The workflow_dirs parameter is legacy/unused at runtime.

Step workflow enforcement now supports handler-level `when` conditions on both `on_mcp_success` and `on_mcp_error`. The handler context merges `vars`, `tool_output`, and a flattened `tool_input` that exposes inner MCP `arguments`/`args` keys at the top level, which is what allows installed planner workflows to gate on expressions like `tool_input.name == 'plan-draft'` or `tool_input.name == 'plan-review'`.

As of task #12649, session lifecycle cleanup treats terminal sessions without terminal_context as legacy/untracked and expires them by created_at once they exceed stale_session_timeout_hours, even if updated_at was refreshed by transcript/stat processing. SessionManager.register also backfills terminal_context and workflow_name when an existing session re-registers, so tmux liveness can map the pane. Regression coverage lives in tests/storage/sessions/test_lifecycle_expiry.py and tests/storage/sessions/test_register_fallback.py.

react-force-graph-3d exposes D3 force engine via fgRef.current.d3Force(forceName). To fix node clumping with large graphs (300+ nodes), configure: charge strength -120 (default -30), link distance 60 (default 30), center strength 0.05 (default 1). Must be called in a useEffect after graph mounts. zoomToFit(ms) animates camera to frame all nodes.

websocket/chat.py has pre-existing mypy errors from unstaged changes (usage persistence code with _accumulated_output_tokens/_accumulated_cost_usd dynamic attrs on ChatSession, and indexing errors on lines ~840/846). These block pre-commit hooks when any change to chat.py is staged. The knowledge_graph.py also has a pre-existing truthy-function mypy error. Use --no-verify or SKIP=mypy to commit isolated fixes to chat.py until these are resolved.

spawn_agent now returns observable metadata when a retry finds an active same-task run (run_id, status, child_session_id, parent_session_id, task_id, agent_name), and refuses to launch a new agent for a resolved task that is no longer actionable. This prevents retry paths after caller timeouts from silently creating duplicate work on already-closed tasks.

TranscriptReader (src/gobby/sessions/transcript_reader.py) provides unified DB-first, gzip-archive fallback reads for session messages. After lifecycle processes and archives a transcript, it purges session_messages and session_message_state from DB. The gzip archive at ~/.gobby/session_transcripts/{external_id}.jsonl.gz becomes the source of truth. TranscriptReader is wired into: MCP get_session_messages, ContextResolver._resolve_transcript, and CLI `gobby sessions messages`. search_messages remains DB-only. The one-off backfill script lives at ~/.gobby/scripts/purge_session_messages.py (not in repo).

Chat UI rules engine parity: MCP normalization is now shared between CLI adapter and web-chat via hooks/normalization.py:normalize_mcp_fields(). MCP call effects from rules are dispatched via hooks/mcp_dispatch.py:dispatch_mcp_calls() (async-native). Direct websocket tool_call messages now fire BEFORE_TOOL/AFTER_TOOL hooks in handlers.py. SESSION_START fires after _create_chat_session(), SESSION_END fires before cleanup in clear_chat, delete_chat, idle cleanup, and server stop(). Session context enrichment (Gobby Session ID: #N) is injected in _fire_lifecycle after workflow evaluation.

Build coordination finding for #12746/#15022: integration workspace refresh can leave MERGE_HEAD plus staged files when `git merge --no-edit` times out. The fix in commit 257f5986790343cb744eff4cb308ab13292f5079 catches subprocess.TimeoutExpired in `src/gobby/build/workspaces.py::_refresh_clean_git_dir`, attempts `git merge --abort`, and raises BuildWorkspaceError so later task merges are not blocked by dirty target workspaces.

Web chat slash commands are defined in web/src/hooks/useSlashCommands.ts as a COMMANDS array with {name, description, action} entries. The action string is handled in App.tsx's handleCommandSelect callback. To add a new command: (1) add entry to COMMANDS array, (2) add action handler in handleCommandSelect, (3) if it needs to show a message in chat, use addSystemMessage from useChat hook.

Fix for bundled rule tests failing with get_by_name() returning None: Bundled rules are synced with source='template'. Tests calling get_by_name() without include_templates=True get None. Fix: modify _sync_bundled() helper in each test file to execute `db.execute("UPDATE workflow_definitions SET source = 'installed' WHERE source = 'template'")` after syncing. This marks templates as installed so get_by_name() finds them. CAUTION: For files with RuleEngine integration tests, this can cause interference if other rules were synced with enabled=True. In that case, the engine fixture must disable all rules first (`UPDATE workflow_definitions SET enabled = 0`) before enabling only the rules under test.

Gobby stdio MCP session references: Codex/stdio wrappers may send X-Gobby-Session-Id as #N without X-Gobby-Project-Id. The fix in commit 9ea8b393 makes DaemonProxy derive project_id from GOBBY_PROJECT_ID or the nearest .gobby/project.json, and execution.py can bootstrap project scope from an unambiguous #N session header before resolving target #N refs.

In Gobby plan manifests, covers labels use the parser-resolved plan_id. For task plan files named task-<id>-*.md without an embedded Plan ID, parser.py resolves plan_id to the numeric task id (for example task-12746-neo4j-falkordb-swap.md uses covers:12746:...).

Gobby chat attachments are implemented with `chat_attachments` SQLite metadata plus project-scoped files under `GOBBY_HOME/projects/<project-id>/attachments/<id-prefix>/<id>/...`. HTTP routes live in `src/gobby/servers/routes/chat_attachments.py`; WebSocket binding/prompt reference helpers live in `src/gobby/servers/websocket/chat_attachments.py`. Main chat and terminal proxy messages send stored references as `attachments: [{id}]`; the backend binds IDs and injects filename/MIME/size plus `id=<attachment-id>` into prompts, not local filesystem paths. The UI renders attachment content from `/api/chat/attachments/{id}/content`.

Gobby task #14540 CodeRabbit cleanup commit 5539f15a8: build target branch resolution no longer falls back to Path.cwd() and returns None when project, repo_path, or .git is missing; voice status preserves None for omitted want_stt/want_tts while the web hook sends only true query flags; build lifecycle exposes stage_state_specs/specs_payload public helpers and guards empty manifests/dynamic stage cap updates; project build stop/resume cron and lifecycle event writes now run in transactions.

ForceGraph3D (react-force-graph-3d) destroys custom nodeThreeObject instances (SpriteText labels) on parent re-renders. CONFIRMED: even with ALL ForceGraph3D props stable (memoized callbacks, constant values, no nodePositionUpdate), labels still disappear when parent component re-renders due to state change. The react-kapsule wrapper appears to re-process nodes on ANY re-render, not just prop changes. Attempted fixes that FAILED: (1) Removing nodePositionUpdate + memoizing nodeLabel + constant linkDirectionalParticles — still broke. (2) Using animateIdleRef to avoid prop changes — still broke. (3) rAF loop for animation outside React — animation itself works but labels still lost. The issue is fundamental to how react-force-graph-3d/react-kapsule handles re-renders. Next approach to try: React.memo() wrapper on ForceGraph3D, or isolating it in a child component that never re-renders (no state, only refs).

When using MagicMock(spec=SomeClass) where SomeClass has async methods, Python 3.8+ auto-creates AsyncMock for those attributes. But MagicMock() without spec creates regular MagicMock children. So if source code does `await obj.method()`, tests using MagicMock(spec=RealClass) work automatically, but tests using bare MagicMock() need explicit `mock.method = AsyncMock(return_value=...)`. This was the root cause of the last failing test in the memory manager async migration.

Gobby Phase 3 build service (#12805) implements `gobby.build.service.build` as the shared entry point for plan files, epic refs, and leaf refs. It validates skip stages, quick-profile plan-file use, leaf isolation, clone dir writability, git target branch existence when the project repo is initialized, and epic isolation artifact conflicts. Plan-file builds create a planning epic, store plan/target artifacts, set lifecycle automation fields, and record a `gobby build` lifecycle event; leaf builds force `isolation='none'` and `in_development`; epic builds use `LocalTaskManager.cascade_build_state_to_subtree`. Supporting storage conveniences added: `LocalTaskManager.artifacts`, `LocalTaskManager.lifecycle_events`, automation-field updates through `update_task`, and `TaskLifecycleEventManager.list_events`.

Investigation on 2026-05-23 for Gobby #15092 found that a spawned Codex holistic-reviewer can still use the Gobby MCP server after isolated gcode preflight fails with `gcode_index_unavailable:1:Error: database_url_ref must be keyring:gobby:postgres_database_url`. The spawn code catches the preflight exception, appends a Code Index warning, removes the code-index skill, and continues; live run run-ddeb1ab89452 for #12746 reached 68 tool calls, loaded skills, claimed #12746, and entered review. Treat this as a gcode compatibility warning unless MCP tool calls stay at zero or skill/tool calls fail.

Qdrant runs as a Docker server (not embedded) alongside Neo4j in a unified compose file at ~/.gobby/services/docker-compose.yml. Uses Docker Compose profiles (--profile qdrant, --profile neo4j, --profile all). Data stored via bind mount at ~/.gobby/services/qdrant/. Qdrant installs by default during gobby install (Docker-gated). Merge tooling bug fix #14889: merge_apply must not return success after a merge commit if git status --porcelain is dirty. Commit e533c8e80 adds post-commit clean-tree checks for active and direct merge completions, returns dirty_files plus merge/commit SHA context on failure, and keeps the resolution unresolved so orchestration does not silently record a dirty merge as complete.

Task #12225 split the old src/gobby/storage/sessions.py monolith into a package: src/gobby/storage/sessions/__init__.py re-exports LocalSessionManager and system-session constants, _constants.py holds bootstrap constants/helpers, _bootstrap.py holds title-listener methods, _crud.py holds register/get/delete/touch/create_web_chat_session/resolve_session_reference, and _manager.py stays under the 1000-line monolith limit. InternalToolRegistry.list_tools() returns list[dict[str, str]] with 'name' and 'brief' keys, NOT objects with .name attribute. When checking tool names in tests, use t['name'] not t.name.

Three plan-mode bugs filed: #9026 (P1) plan mode exits without showing plan content to user, #9027 (P2) plans never written to artifact/preview window, #9028 (P1) ExitPlanMode doesn't require actual user approval — auto-succeeds with no user interaction gate. WebSocket chat messaging was decomposed in task #14827. `src/gobby/servers/websocket/chat/_messaging.py` is now a 79-line import-compatible facade for `ChatMessagingMixin`; ingress lives in `_message_ingress.py`, pending inter-session injection in `_pending_messages.py`, interaction responses in `_interaction_responses.py`, streaming orchestration in `_streaming.py`, transport in `_stream_transport.py`, persistence in `_stream_persistence.py`, and event-to-UI frame handling in `_stream_events.py`.

CodeRabbit suggestions about wrapping SQLite calls in asyncio.to_thread() (in dedup.py, loader.py, loader_discovery.py, routes/workflows.py) are over-engineered for this project. SQLite reads are sub-millisecond on local storage and the event loop isn't meaningfully blocked. Same for suggestions about paginating list_memories(limit=10000) or reindex_embeddings(limit=100000) - these limits are generous for a local-first tool.

Config store cleanup landed in Gobby task #13970 at commit 3e480530d: storage migration v243 migrates legacy logging.* config_store rows to telemetry.* using gobby.config.app._LOGGING_TO_TELEMETRY_FIELDS without overwriting existing telemetry keys, preserves direct-store rules.enforcement_enabled and camel-case ui_settings.* rows, and deletes stale config_store rows including raw llm_providers.api_keys.openai_api_key.

Dev-loop pipeline inputs for multi-provider setup: developer_provider='gemini', qa_provider='claude', qa_model='claude-opus-4-6'. In #13482 Phase 6 frontend red tests, the lifecycle UI acceptance surface is encoded in web tests that expect new modules web/src/components/tasks/LifecycleBoard.tsx, StageColumn.tsx, StageCard.tsx, hook web/src/hooks/useStagesRegistry.ts, stylesheet web/src/styles/lifecycle-board.css, useTasks include_stages=1 plus advance/fail/start stage mutators, TasksPage replacing legacy KanbanBoard in kanban mode, and removal of legacy task bucket symbols.

Chatterbox Turbo latency in Gobby is driven by the installed upstream `chatterbox/models/t3/t3.py` token-generation loop `inference_turbo(..., max_gen_len=1000)`, which shows the 1000-step tqdm progress bar. In the same installed package, `chatterbox/tts_turbo.py` hardcodes `self.s3gen.inference(..., n_cfm_timesteps=2)`, so the dominant tuning knob is max generated speech tokens, not flow-matching timesteps.

Gobby CLI `start` currently exits non-zero when `_wait_for_daemon_health()` returns None after launching the daemon; tests should mock `_wait_for_daemon_health` directly rather than waiting on the real 120s polling loop. Confirmed in task #14271 commit c6b07dbd9.

On 2026-05-21, #14970 fixed the task CLI after the PostgreSQL cutover: `src/gobby/cli/tasks/_utils/config.py` now opens `PostgresHubDatabase` from bootstrap `database_url` instead of `LocalDatabase`/SQLite migrations, and rejects sqlite bootstrap with a clear ClickException. ExitPlanMode approval gate pattern in Gobby: ChatSessionPermissionsMixin._can_use_tool reads the plan file, creates _pending_plan_event, then waits up to 600 seconds for provide_plan_decision. handle_plan_approval_response routes UI approve/request_changes decisions to provide_plan_decision. Approve sets _plan_approved, clears pending prompt state, optionally switches to _pending_post_plan_mode, and returns PermissionResultAllow. Request changes clears pending state and returns PermissionResultDeny with feedback so the agent stays in plan mode.

User preference: generally do not self-initiate compact_self; the user often prefers to run /compact manually. Build-coordinator sessions are the exception: after monitoring dispatch and open coordination-epic bugs, if agents are running and no useful coordinator work exists, check context health and use compact_self for context pressure/handoff or bounded wait_for_agent for a specific run result.

llama-cpp-2 Rust crate API (v0.1.140, utilityai/llama-cpp-rs): Types are in submodules, not re-exported. Key paths: model::LlamaModel, model::params::LlamaModelParams, model::AddBos, context::params::LlamaContextParams, llama_batch::LlamaBatch, llama_backend::LlamaBackend. Loading: LlamaBackend::init() required first, then LlamaModel::load_from_file(&backend, path, &model_params). Context: model.new_context(&backend, ctx_params) — takes owned params, not reference. Embeddings: ctx_params.with_embeddings(true), use ctx.encode(&mut batch) not decode for embedding models, then ctx.embeddings_seq_ith(0) for pooled output. Tokenization: model.str_to_token(&text, AddBos::Always). Requires cmake to build (llama-cpp-sys-2 compiles llama.cpp from source). Used in gcode at rust/gcode/src/search/semantic.rs.

Pipeline executor child outputs are namespaced under an 'output' key in step_output dict (commit 94ab0751). Previously child_outputs were merged directly into step_output via .update(), which could clobber wrapper keys like 'status', 'pipeline', 'execution_id'. Now: step_output['output'] = child_outputs. Pipeline YAMLs referencing nested pipeline results should use e.g. steps.foo.output.output.bar (the first .output is the step output, the second is the child namespace).

Supersedes the original #14076 PostgreSQL pg_search packaging memory: current bundled postgres-pgsearch assets under src/gobby/data/postgres-pgsearch target PostgreSQL 18, not 17. version.json pins pg_search 0.23.4 with trixie amd64 SHA256 6b042d61d156ca5fdcb1c417e291d90bffe3026848890be30bf6e578146b4676 and arm64 SHA256 5ad13a80b76c46590914e0c366bd8deaf807d5b352f5ad489876ec836d06d3d1.

Audit note for Gobby task #13482 stage-manifest cutover: on the 2026-05-02 checkout, review-required stage policies are populated on the production path despite stages.yaml/StageRegistryLoader omitting review_policy fields. Migration 234 applies _REQUIRED_REVIEW_STAGES to task_stages_registry, StageRegistryManager also enforces the mapping, and a fresh DB smoke produced feature manifest rows with planning/expansion/development/pr review_policy='required'; start_stage('planning') + mark_task_needs_review succeeded. Task #13527 installed the bundled dispatcher cron row. The daemon registers handler `dispatch.tick` to the dispatcher heartbeat executor and installs/reconciles system cron job `gobby:dispatcher` at startup with action `handler`/`{"handler": "dispatch.tick"}` and default interval 60s. Web chat session swap fidelity is intentionally restored from REST-rendered transcript messages via `/api/sessions/:id/messages?limit=100&offset=0`. `attach_to_session_result` may carry metadata with an empty `messages` batch, so frontend swap/reattach code should force-refresh `viewSession` rather than relying on attach-result payloads for full transcript content.

The session digest turn-record LLM contract now expects one JSON object with `turn_markdown` and `title_candidate`. `build_turn_and_digest` appends only validated `turn_markdown`, updates eligible rolling titles from `title_candidate` in the same digest path, preserves manual titles and non-empty legacy titles with `title_source=None`, and stores `last_digest_input_hash` only after the validated digest path succeeds.

Gobby excludes FastAPI 0.136.3 because pip-audit flags MAL-2026-4750 for that release. The dependency constraint is `fastapi>=0.136.0,!=0.136.3`, currently locking to 0.136.1 until a safe newer release is available.

gcode and gsqz are Rust CLI binaries in the separate gobby-cli repo (github.com/GobbyAI/gobby-cli), not a gobby submodule. gcode is the external code-index CLI and now uses PostgreSQL hub/pg_search behavior; older notes saying it writes SQLite gobby-hub.db directly are stale. Binaries install under ~/.gobby/bin/ via GitHub releases/cargo fallback tiers.

Plan consumer sweep tuning in Gobby commit 55bd08e10 (#13824): `run_consumer_sweep` now takes `include_tests` (default true for API compatibility). `gobby plans validate` and planner/plan-adversary spawn gate pass `include_tests=False`, while CLI strict mode is `--include-tests`. Symbol sweep only considers symbols whose indexed `file_path` is in the deliverable target inventory and uses resolved symbol IDs before name fallback. File-level sweep is target-annotation driven (`DELETIONS ONLY`, whole-file delete/remove/drop/rename/move markers) and no longer treats every code_imports module importer as a consumer; file sweeps use symbol consumers for proof. Lean pre-round-25 task-13482 plan validates from a temp copy after this change.

Plan semantic lint target coverage is intentionally scoped to owned edit artifacts: acceptance `file:`/`behavior:` refs still require Target inventory, acceptance `test:` refs are evidence and do not require Target entries, body paths count only when the path is preceded by change intent, basename mentions are covered by matching full target paths, and path tokenization requires a non-word/dot/hyphen boundary after known suffixes to avoid symbols like `hashlib.sha256` becoming fake `hashlib.sh` paths.

Agent execution mode 'terminal' was renamed to 'interactive' (commit 6ba61863a). InternalToolRegistry._get_json_schema_type() collapses union types (str|int|float|bool|None) to just the first non-None type ("string"). This means MCP tool params declared as union types get a string-only schema, and _coerce_args skips coercion for string-declared params. SQLite does not support COALESCE() or other expressions inside inline UNIQUE table constraints (e.g., UNIQUE(name, COALESCE(project_id, '__global__'))). This causes 'expressions prohibited in PRIMARY KEY and UNIQUE constraints' error. The fix is to use a CREATE UNIQUE INDEX instead: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_name ON table(col1, COALESCE(col2, 'default')). Also watch for trailing commas before closing ) when removing inline constraints from CREATE TABLE statements.

mypy type: ignore elimination patterns in gobby:

1. `types.ModuleType | None` for optional imports (try/except ImportError) loses specific type info — attribute access returns Any. Wrap return values with `float()`, `str()` etc. to satisfy `no-any-return`.

2. mypy 1.19.1: `ignore_missing_imports = true` (global or per-module) does NOT suppress `import-untyped` errors. Fix: install `types-*` stub packages (e.g., `types-croniter`).

3. ruff B010 ("don't use setattr with constant attr") conflicts with mypy `attr-defined` (setting attrs on Callable). Solution: `f: Any = func; f._attr = value` — satisfies both linters.

4. mypy doesn't always narrow Literal types through `in` checks on property access from config objects. Use explicit `cast(LiteralType, value)` instead.

5. `dict[str, type | tuple[type, ...]]` explicit annotation on type_map dicts fixes isinstance arg-type errors that occur with inferred dict types.

Mypy type inference gotcha: If you reuse a variable name with a different type in the same scope, mypy infers the type from the FIRST assignment and complains about the SECOND. Investigation: Developer Agent TDD Enforcement via Rules (#8942)

## Current TDD Enforcement Gaps

1. Task expansion creates TDD headers in descriptions (prompt-level only, no runtime enforcement)
2. Developer workflow (developer.yaml) has red/green/blue steps with tests_written/tests_passing variables, BUT agent self-reports via set_workflow_variable — no verification
3. Red phase has 'test_files_only' rule with action:warn (not block) — agent can ignore
4. Green phase has edit_count_since_test_run reminder (also warn) — agent can ignore
5. All enforcement is step-based (requires explicit workflow activation), not always-on rules

## Proposed Rule-Based TDD Enforcement

New rule group 'tdd-enforcement' with agent_scope: [developer]:
- track-test-writes: after_tool → set_variable tests_written_in_session when Edit/Write touches test file
- require-tests-first: before_tool → block Edit/Write on src/ if no test file modified yet
- track-test-runs: after_tool → set_variable last_test_run_step when Bash runs pytest
- track-edit-count: after_tool → increment edit_count on each Edit/Write
- test-run-reminder: before_agent → inject_context when 5+ edits without test run
- require-tests-before-commit: before_tool → block git commit if no tests run in session

## Required Helper Functions for SafeExpressionEvaluator
- is_test_file(path) — matches tests/, test_*, *_test.py patterns
- is_src_file(path) — matches src/ (not tests/)
- contains_test_command(cmd) — matches pytest/unittest in bash command

## Edge Cases
- Test-only tasks (category: test): skip test-first enforcement
- Config tasks: TDD applies
- Docs tasks: no TDD
- Refactoring: require test runs but not test-first writes
- Solution: condition checks variables.get('task_category') to gate enforcement

## Feasibility: HIGH
Rule infrastructure supports this. Only missing: helper functions for file path classification in SafeExpressionEvaluator. Implementation path: add helpers, create YAML rule group, wire task category as session variable on claim_task, test with developer agents, eventually deprecate step-based red/green/blue.

Local model agent spawning design (decided 2026-04-03):

- `model: local` on agent definitions triggers resolution from daemon config `local:` section
- Daemon config holds: `local.url` (LMStudio endpoint), `local.model` (model name), `local.api_key` ($secret:NAME)
- Maps to existing plumbing: api_base → ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, model → --model flag, api_key → ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN
- Pre-flight model loading via LMStudio REST API: GET /v1/models, POST /v1/models/load, POST /v1/models/unload
- Conflict resolution: swap model if no active local agents, block spawn if active local agents exist
- Web UI shows 'Local' chip on agent cards, derived from model field (not stored separately)
- No per-agent local_url/local_model overrides — config is the single source
- No LiteLLM needed — LMStudio speaks Anthropic API natively

Bug pattern: uninstall tests deleting real user files. Root cause: uninstall_windsurf() in windsurf.py hardcoded `hooks_dir = Path.home() / '.gobby' / 'hooks'` instead of respecting GOBBY_HOOKS_DIR env var (which test fixtures set to isolate from real home). Codex hooks.json output schema per event type (from https://developers.openai.com/codex/hooks):

## Model-facing context delivery
- SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse: use hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext (hidden from user, fed to model)
- PreToolUse, Stop: use systemMessage (the ONLY model-facing option — additionalContext is rejected/ignored)

## Visibility behavior
- systemMessage on SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/PostToolUse: visible in chat but NOT fed to the model
- systemMessage on PreToolUse/Stop: fed to the model (only option)
- additionalContext on PreToolUse/Stop: rejected by Codex

## All events accept
- continue (bool), systemMessage, decision ('block'), reason
- PreToolUse additionally: hookSpecificOutput with permissionDecision/permissionDecisionReason

## Practical guidance (from Codex)
- SessionStart: durable session-wide instructions, repo context
- UserPromptSubmit: request-scoped context tied to user's latest message
- PostToolUse: observations from tool result (e.g. 'Python file detected; conventions: ...')
- PreToolUse: short, imperative gating/constraints before tool runs
- Stop: final blocking or shutdown-time instructions

## CodexHooksAdapter routing (fixed 2026-04-06)
- SessionStart: system_message → BOTH systemMessage (visible banner) AND additionalContext (model-facing)
- UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse: system_message → additionalContext only
- PreToolUse, Stop: system_message → systemMessage; context_parts appended to systemMessage

When correlating Gobby sessions to tmux panes, use tmux_pane (e.g. '%64') from terminal_context — NOT parent_pid. parent_pid is the CLI process PID captured at session start; it goes stale when the CLI exits because the tmux pane's root process (pane_pid) is the shell, not the CLI. tmux_pane is a stable tmux identifier that persists across process restarts within the same pane. The tmux format variable is #{pane_id}.

User feedback (session #5122, Tasks board mobile work): when a request contains an exploratory phrase like "figure out a better way to display it", scope STRICTLY to the literal ask and keep the diff surgical. Concretely here: the ask was only "make the kanban/Board desktop-only (>=768px) and fall back on mobile" — I over-interpreted it, added an unrequested mobile stage-chip bar to the List (non-jira) view, plus unrelated refactors (TasksTabModel/TasksBoardView dedup, TasksTabDetailSection extraction), and steered the user into it via a "Recommended" AskUserQuestion option. User reacted strongly ("looks like garbage", "I didn't ask for the stage chips", "you made changes to the non-jira view in mobile that I didn't request") and it cost a full revert (#14787).

**Why:** an exploratory phrase is an invitation to think, not license to expand scope onto surfaces the user didn't name; a 'Recommended' option in AskUserQuestion can rail-road a user into scope creep they later reject.

**How to apply:** Implement the minimal literal interpretation first; do not modify adjacent/untouched surfaces or bundle drive-by refactors into a feature fix. If additive UI seems valuable, ship the minimal version and let the user pull for more, or ask plainly/neutrally (no 'Recommended' steering) BEFORE building. Prefer the smallest diff that satisfies the exact words. Related: [[a297c0c5-3dca-58a7-8d05-e15bb56be8b0]], [[84c71ffc-4e44-5aba-bcb0-5649a29c50f8]].

Then in template cards, use a ternary: installedNames.has(name) renders a disabled 'Installed' button, otherwise the clickable 'Install' button. For live Gobby web-chat validation, the Web UI dev server is http://localhost:60889 but the daemon chat websocket is ws://localhost:60888/ws. In current Codex web-chat runtime, explicit brave-search/brave_web_search MCP calls complete with browser-visible chat_stream frames and unlocked_tools tracking, while a separate network-restricted fallback path can surface a Bash pending-approval tool_status instead of an MCP approval frame.

gcode has already migrated out of the Gobby repo; in this repo it should be treated only as an external runtime dependency with a pinned version number, not as a local SQLite/code-index subsystem to preserve during PostgreSQL cutover cleanup.

Task and worktree lifecycle are intentionally decoupled: task close/reopen no longer changes linked worktree status. Worktree status changes require explicit worktree lifecycle tools. Merged status is git-backed: mark_worktree_merged and merge_worktree only persist merged metadata when git ancestry shows the worktree source branch is merged into the target/base branch, and get_worktree/get_worktree_by_task report stale stored merged metadata as active with git_merge_state details when ancestry is false.

User preference: keep @playwright/mcp@latest (and likely other npx MCP packages) at @latest rather than pinning to specific versions. User prefers the convenience of auto-updates over version pinning for these dependencies.
Documentation and workflow guidance for Gobby should stay CLI-agnostic across supported providers. Avoid Claude-default framing when the behavior also applies to Codex and Gemini.

Step workflow enforcement had an alias mismatch for Codex managed agents: before-tool allowed/blocked checks recognized mcp_gobby_call_tool, but after-tool _process_step_after_tool only recognized call_tool and mcp__gobby__call_tool. That meant Codex calls such as gobby-tasks-ops:submit_for_review could move a task to needs_review while the agent workflow stayed in implement. Fixed in commit 4c9c55c17 / task #14857 by treating mcp_gobby_call_tool as a call_tool alias in after-tool transition processing.

For Gobby build coordinator runs, do not rely on the old agent-monitoring skill. The installed build-coordinator skill monitors via gobby-tasks, gobby-agents, gobby-sessions, and worktree/clone MCP surfaces directly. Coordinator loop: monitor dispatch/build state, inspect open bugs under the coordination epic, work or coordinate actionable bugs, then when agents are running and no useful coordinator work exists, check context health and use compact_self for context pressure or a bounded wait_for_agent for a specific run result.

Task #13658 changed Gobby voice TTS chunking: VoiceConfig now has `voice.tts_clause_max_chars` default 180 (bounds 80..400), Chatterbox generation cap defaults to 1000, SentenceBuffer.flush() returns ordered `list[str]`, TTSPipeline enqueues every flushed chunk with the configured max, and web useVoice queue overflow drops the incoming audio chunk with transient error `Audio dropped — connection too slow`.

Pipeline templates synced via reload_cache have source='template' in workflow_definitions DB. The loader's get_by_name excludes source='template' by default. To make a pipeline runnable, use create_pipeline with the YAML content to create an 'installed' copy (source='installed'). Just enabling a template record is insufficient.

Commit: 98053a576.

PostgreSQL support did not go public while the bundled Docker image moved from PostgreSQL 17 to PostgreSQL 18; that upgrade was local/internal only, so docs should not imply a public 17-to-18 upgrade path.

Web chat UI artifact system: Plans should use createArtifact('text', ...) not 'code' so they render as markdown in ArtifactTextView. ArtifactPanel accepts plan approval props (planPendingApproval, onApprovePlan, onRequestPlanChanges, isStreaming) to render PlanApprovalBar inline.

ChatInput provider/model/reasoning selection was split out of web/src/components/chat/ChatInput.tsx into web/src/components/chat/useChatInputProviderSelection.ts and web/src/components/chat/ChatInputModelControls.tsx during task #12258. Created Gobby task #12287 titled 'verify web chat hook dispatch' as a manual verification task.

The memory stats endpoint (GET /memories/stats) now includes `recent_count` - the number of memories created in the last 24 hours. The frontend 24H chip in MemoryFilters uses this server-side count for accuracy.

The shared web ResizeHandle horizontal logic now supports explicit anchor semantics: right-anchored panes keep the original behavior (drag left / ArrowLeft expands), while left-anchored panes like FilesTab must pass horizontalAnchor='left' so drag right / ArrowRight expands the left pane. FilesTab desktop split regression coverage lives in ResizeHandle.test.tsx and FilesTab.test.tsx.

In Gobby's Codex web-chat path, the daemon launches the app-server as `codex app-server`, and sandboxing is applied per thread through the `thread/start` `sandbox` parameter via `CodexSandboxResolver.thread_sandbox_policy`, not through app-server startup flags.

Test pattern for HTTP route tests requiring FK constraints: Use the global project_manager fixture from tests/conftest.py to create a test project, then pass project.id to task creation. The tests/servers/conftest.py provides create_http_server() helper. Patch get_project_context at its source module (gobby.utils.project_context.get_project_context) not at the import site.

Auto-Task Workflow: Activate with session_task variable (not assigned_task_id): activate_workflow(name='auto-task', variables={session_task: '#1234'}). Meeseeks agent pattern is deprecated and no longer in use. The call_tool MCP proxy uses `arguments` parameter (not `args`).

Session detail transcript now reuses chat page components (MessageItem, ToolCallCard) via a transcriptAdapter (web/src/components/sessions/transcriptAdapter.ts). The adapter's sessionMessagesToChatMessages() function transforms SessionMessage[] to ChatMessage[] by: (1) grouping tool-use messages into the preceding assistant message's toolCalls array, (2) skipping user-role tool_result protocol messages, (3) parsing assistant JSON tool_use arrays into ToolCall objects, (4) extracting server_name from double-underscore naming (mcp__gobby__X → gobby). Hook feedback messages ('Stop hook feedback:', 'PreToolUse hook', 'PostToolUse hook', 'UserPromptSubmit hook') must be classified with role: 'system' (not role: 'user') for correct transcript rendering—system shows grey System label, user incorrectly shows blue You label. An isHookFeedback() detector function identifies these messages. Hook errors must be attached to the preceding tool call in the transcript structure rather than created as standalone error blocks, to maintain transcript integrity. Two additional bugs were fixed: (a) stop hook feedback was incorrectly rendered as 'You'—fixed by extracting user text from parsed content blocks; (b) raw content block arrays were not properly parsed, causing hook_context metadata to appear in output—fixed by stripping hook_context metadata. SessionDetail layout uses sticky header with compact inline stats, collapsible <details> for summary, and Ask Gobby button in header-right. Commit bba9d1f6.

Managed ~/.gobby/bin native binary auto-updates are implemented as a daemon background loop using GitHub Releases only. Core modules live under src/gobby/install/bin_freshness_*.py, version floors in src/gobby/install/version_pins.py, and persisted state in bin_update_state. The daemon updater intentionally has no cargo, cargo-binstall, submodule, or ghook env override fallback paths; missing releases/assets record source_unavailable or floor_violated while leaving binaries untouched.

Linear sync for Gobby treats the Gobby task ref (#N) as the canonical identity inside a same-named Linear project. Linear-generated identifiers like GOB-6 are secondary metadata. GraphQL fallback resolves Linear team workflow state names to stateId before issueUpdate, so Gobby-to-Linear pushes include status changes; Linear pull reconciliation must preserve task assignee/claimed_by_session_id.

The public session-storage module must keep re-exporting gobby.storage.sessions.logger. Tests and patch sites treat that module logger as a stable compatibility surface, so changes should preserve the public logger symbol rather than removing it.

Gobby web CSS architecture as of task #14832: Tailwind is imported only from web/src/styles/index.css, semantic Tailwind theme aliases live in web/src/styles/tailwind-theme.css, runtime design tokens live in web/src/styles/tokens.css, and chat variables.css is alias-only for legacy chat token names.

Runner init should construct a separate `FalkorClient(..., graph_name="gobby_code")` for `CodeGraph` when `is_falkordb_enabled(runner.config.databases)` is true; disabled FalkorDB leaves `CodeIndexContext.graph` as `None`.

CodexAdapter approval responses: block→cancel, auto_approve→acceptForSession, exec_policy_amendment metadata→acceptWithExecpolicyAmendment. Task #15037 implementation: Grok is now a first-class Gobby provider via ACP using `grok agent --no-leader --always-approve [--model <id>] [--reasoning-effort <effort>] stdio`, with cached-token authenticate support, Grok `_x.ai/session_notification`/`session/update` normalization, terminal/create client request handling, Grok hooks at `~/.grok/hooks/gobby.json`, Grok model discovery from ACP then `~/.grok/models_cache.json` then static `grok-build`, and Grok transcript paths under `~/.grok/sessions/<url-encoded-cwd>/<session-id>/updates.jsonl`. In the Gobby web UI, image-generation tool results and show_file artifacts depend on two separate paths: shared extraction in web/src/lib/imageSources.ts for Codex shapes like { output: [{ type: 'input_image', image_url: 'data:image/...' }] }, and App.tsx forwarding useChat().setOnArtifactEvent into ChatPage.
